mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the cost of capital and increase equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the 20-day periods following months with FEDFUNDS below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.8%) signals strong labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the 20-day periods following months with UNRATE < 4.8%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the 20-day periods when both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the 20-day periods during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%).

mechanism_narrative: A higher industrial production level (INDPRO) is causally linked to stronger economic activity and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the 60-day periods following months with INDPRO above 120.0.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1.5% signals economic weakness that triggers risk-off sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the 20-day periods following quarters with GDPC1 growth < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the 5-day periods when PAYEMS increases by more than 100k and UNRATE falls by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation environments (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to central bank tightening and real rate pressures, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the 60-day periods during high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized).
